metadata.case_name: LAI TIM FAI JACKY v. LEE YUK PING

plaintiff.occupation_after: apprenticed roast-meat worker; part-time roast-meat worker; van attendant; waiter; vehicle attendant

injuries.description: multiple skull fracture and subdural haematoma.
source: multiple skull fracture and subdural haematoma.

injuries.description: severe open brain injuries; brain contusion; extensive left side skull fractures
source: Diagnosis was of severe open brain injuries
CT brain scan showed extensive left side skull fractures and brain contusion.

injuries.description: 18cm ragged laceration of left frontal-temporal-parietal scalp
source: 18cm ragged laceration of left frontal-temporal-parietal scalp, active arterial bleeding and skull bone fragments were found in the wound.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration with foreign body of head

source: Gross dysphonia was evident and the ENT specialist found his left vocal cord was paralysed, presumably as a result of the head trauma.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified peripheral nerves of neck

injuries.description: damage to the visual pathway causing marked constriction of the visual fields (loss of peripheral vision)
source: marked constriction of the visual fields, more severe in the right eye, due to damage to the visual pathway.
losses of 72% and 70% of visual field for the right and left eyes respectively
injuries.icd_description: Injury of optic tract or pathways, bilateral

injuries.description: epilepsy as a sequelae of his severe brain injury (post-traumatic epilepsy / continuing risk of epileptic seizure)
source: he has to take anticonvulsants on a regular basis for epilepsy as a sequelae of his severe brain injury
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: speech remained weak; slow speech and responses; stutters
marked constriction of the visual fields (loss of peripheral vision)
impairment of orientation, concentration, calculation, memory, general knowledge, and abstract thinking
global cognitive impairment and psychomotor retardation
poor memory, slow response; inability to co-ordinate movements sufficiently to play video games
unable to pursue activities such as football, snooker, swimming and other games
poor physical and mental stamina; need for supervision; poor concentration; poor problem solving; poor judgment; lack of accuracy in visual discrimination

treatments_received: admitted to the Tuen Mun Hospital and transferred to the neurosurgical unit of the Prince of Wales Hospital
wound debridement, haemostasis and intracranial pressure monitoring
ventilatory support in the intensive care unit
craniectomy to evacuate reaccumulated haematomas (two further operations)
operation on his skull to close a gap in the bone with an artificial flap (1994)
rehabilitation at Cheshire Home and convalescent hospital

losses.description: Residual damage to eyesight with marked constriction of the visual fields; losses of visual field assessed at 72% (right) and 70% (left).
Global cognitive impairment, impairment of orientation, concentration, calculation, memory, general knowledge, and abstract thinking; psychomotor retardation.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to pursue activities such as football, snooker, swimming and other games which he used to enjoy before the accident.
Loss of the satisfaction in his trade as a mechanic and consequent confinement to occupations of the most menial nature.
